title: Phone Area Code Map: NANP Codes by State
description: Browse NANP area codes by US state with the Phone Area Code Map — overlays and portability explained for support and marketing checks. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, 212 still whispers old Manhattan, but number portability means the phone itself might now live in Florida — the map gives the code's home, not the handset's.
quick_answer: The Phone Area Code Map lists NANP area codes by US state for support and marketing checks. Choose a state and read its codes — original splits and modern overlays together — with portability's caveat: a code names where a number was born, not where its owner stands.
steps_intro: Area codes are geography with an expiry date. Read them properly:

Campaign lists by area code still sketch territories — overlays mean one city, several codes, all listed here together.
A 'local' caller whose code belongs three states away is a flag, not a verdict — the map supplies the flag.
Old letterheads and ads carry dead codes; the map's state association dates and places them.
Miami answers to 305 and its overlay 786; Manhattan holds 212 with 646 and 332 stacked on the same streets. The map lists a state's codes together — the only honest way to show modern numbering.
Since US wireless portability (2003), people keep numbers across moves and states. A 312 number rings in Austin now. The code is the number's biography, first chapter only.

popular_table.title: Famous codes and their ground
popular_table.intro: A sampler of the map's associations — the codes everyone recognises, with their overlays' lesson.
popular_table.note: The NANP covers the US, Canada and parts of the Caribbean under one plan — this map's browsing focus is US states, as the support and marketing use cases are.

faq: It qualifies it: an area code reliably names where a number was first assigned, and porting lets owners keep numbers anywhere. Use the map for origin and territory logic, not for a person's current location.
Can I use the tool without sharing my precise location?
Yes — nothing here locates you; states are chosen, not detected.
Why might a boundary or place name look different elsewhere?
Numbering areas split and overlay on administrators' schedules; other sources may list a brand-new overlay earlier or later.
Does MapBench store my browser location?
No — and this page never asks for it.
A second code serving the same ground as an original, added when numbers ran low. Overlay areas require ten-digit dialing for local calls.
Canada shares the NANP (416 Toronto, 604 Vancouver and their overlays), but this page's browsing is organised by US states.
Can an area code cross state lines?
A few do, near borders. The map associates codes with the states they serve, plural where the numbering plan says so.
800, 888, 877 and kin are non-geographic and excluded from a state map by design.
How do I find one address's area code?
Resolve the address's state and city with the address tools, then read its codes here — remembering overlays make several answers correct.
